question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Percentage Error of an Approximation
question.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.98)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(2+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to one decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem for positive integer $n$ states that

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

By substituting $a=2,$ $b=x,$ and $n=5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(2+x)}^{5} & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{0}){(2)}^{5}{(x)}^{0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}){(2)}^{5-1}{(x)}^{1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2}){(2)}^{5-2}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1{(2)}^{5}+5{(2)}^{4}{(x)}^{1}+10{(2)}^{3}{(x)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1(32)+5(16)(x)+10(8)({x}^{2})+⋯ \\  & =32+80x+80{x}^{2}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(2+x)}^{5}≈32+80x+80{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=-0.02$ into the above approximation of $(2+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.98)^{5} & =(2+(-0.02))^{5} \\  & ≈32+80(-0.02)+80(-0.02)^{2} \\  & =32-80(0.02)+80(0.000\,4) \\  & =32-1.6+0.032 \\  & =30.432\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.98)^{5}-30.432|}{(1.98)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.0%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
